tiebreak_notes: Canceled game: the Week 17 BUF at CIN game was canceled, not resumed, so BUF (13-3) and CIN (12-4) played 16 games. Seeding was by winning percentage: KC .824 > BUF .8125 for No. 1. CIN won the AFC North over BAL (10-7) on winning percentage (.750 vs .588); per Wikipedia, 'By canceling the game, the Bengals automatically clinched the AFC North division championship based on winning percentage.'

Special resolution (NFL owners, Jan 2023): it did not change any seed. (a) Because BUF and KC both won in Week 18, a BUF-KC AFC Championship would have been played at a neutral site (Atlanta). It never happened, since CIN beat BUF in the Divisional round. (b) A coin toss for home field in a BAL-CIN wild-card game would have applied only if BAL had beaten CIN in Week 18. CIN won, so no toss was needed and No. 3 CIN hosted No. 6 BAL.
AFC No. 5 seed (LAC vs BAL, both 10-7): 'LA Chargers claimed the No. 5 seed over Baltimore based on conference record (7-5 vs. 6-6).' [The 2022-23 NFL playoffs Wikipedia page says the same.]
AFC No. 7 seed (MIA vs PIT, both 9-8): 'Miami finished ahead of Pittsburgh based on head-to-head victory, claiming the 7th and final playoff spot.'
NFC No. 2 seed (SF vs MIN, both 13-4): 'San Francisco claimed the No. 2 seed over Minnesota based on conference record (10-2 vs. 8-4).'
NFC No. 7 seed (SEA vs DET, both 9-8): 'Seattle finished ahead of Detroit based on head-to-head victory, claiming the 7th and final playoff spot.'
NYG (9-7-1) got No. 6 on winning percentage (.559), ahead of the 9-8 teams; no tiebreaker was needed.
